stories.headline: Army reviews operational preparedness along LoC in J&K’s Poonch district
stories.title: Army reviews operational preparedness along LoC in J&K’s Poonch district

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

Jammu: General Officer Commanding (GOC) of the Army’s Nagrota-headquartered White Knight Corps, Lt General Mohit Seth, on Saturday visited the line of control (LoC) in J&K’s Poonch district to review the operational preparedness of the formation.
“The #CorpsCommander was briefed on the prevailing security environment, counter-infiltration measures, surveillance architecture and ongoing initiatives to further enhance operational effectiveness.
Commending the troops for their unwavering commitment and operational excellence, the #GOC impressed upon all ranks to maintain highest standards of Vigilance, readiness and responsiveness.
“We Serve.
We Protect!”
Lieutenant General Mohit Seth took over command of the Nagrota-based White Knight Corps on Thursday from Lieutenant General PK Mishra.
Lt-Gen Seth, an Infantry officer, served as Commandant of the Indian Military Training Team (IMTRAT) in Bhutan before taking over command of the 16 Corps.

On assuming command, the new Corps Commander exhorted all ranks to uphold the highest standards of operational readiness, professional excellence and team spirit, while continuing to foster peace, security and stability in the region.
“Prepared For Today, Ready For Tomorrow.
We Serve, We Protect,” White Knight Corps said in a post on X.
An alumnus of the National Defence Academy, Khadakwasla and the National Defence College, New Delhi, Lt Gen Seth was commissioned into the Third Battalion of the Madras Regiment in 1991.

stories.headline: Madurantakam by-election: Will the AIADMK ‘bastion’ fall to TVK’s growing popularity?
stories.title: Madurantakam by-election: Will the AIADMK ‘bastion’ fall to TVK’s growing popularity?
stories.summary: Maragatham Kumaravel, a former AIADMK leader, now seeks re-election as the TVK’s candidate after resigning as AIADMK MLA barely three weeks after the 2026 result; while some voters are undecided, some say they may not vote for the TVK despite the CM’s popularity
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In the 2021 Assembly Elections, the ruling AIADMK was swept away by a DMK wave in the KTCC districts (Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, and Chennai), barring one single seat – Madurantakam.
Maragatham Kumaravel, a seasoned AIADMK leader and a Lok Sabha member for the party during 2014-19 period, stood tall among the ruins.
She regained the seat in the 2026 elections amid a TVK wave in the region, giving rise to claims that it was an AIADMK bastion.
Then came the twist.
Barely three weeks after the declaration of results, Ms. Maragatham, along with five of her colleagues, resigned from the Assembly and joined the TVK.
She is now recast as the TVK candidate for the Madurantakam by-election scheduled for October 6.
On Friday, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay held a four-and-a-half-hour-long roadshow in the constituency.
People lined up in large numbers all along the route, which crisscrossed the constituency touching about three dozen villages.
If the turnout of people translates to votes for the party, the TVK would win.
But often, what is apparent isn’t real, warns Ashok, a grocery store owner in Ayyanar Nagar.
“Not all those who gather at Vijay’s rallies would vote for TVK.
I went there too to catch a glimpse of him but I may not vote for them,” he states.

stories.headline: RBI repo rate: Crisil says India Inc can absorb 50-bps rate hike as corporate balance sheets remain strong
stories.title: RBI repo rate: Crisil says India Inc can absorb 50-bps rate hike as corporate balance sheets remain strong
stories.summary: Crisil Ratings said a rate hike of up to 50 basis points would be largely manageable for India Inc, although some sectors could face pressure.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'repo rate' in title weight 42
article_sentences: Its sensitivity analysis found that a 25-basis-point rate hike would reduce median interest coverage by only around 10 basis points, while a 50-basis-point increase would lower it by about 20 basis points.
Under its scenarios, interest coverage could remain around 5.1 times in the event of a 25-basis-point hike and around 5.0 times with a 50-basis-point increase.

Crisil also noted that previous rate-hike cycles have had limited impact on the credit profiles of sectors, suggesting that corporate balance-sheet strength can provide a buffer during periods of higher borrowing costs.
Infrastructure sectors are expected to remain broadly resilient even if rates rise.
Crisil said strong debt-protection metrics, tariff pass-through mechanisms and healthy demand would provide support.
However, commercial real estate could see a moderate impact on debt-service coverage ratios in a 50-basis-point rate-hike scenario.
India Inc’s overall credit-quality outlook for FY27.
The potential impact of higher rates comes against a backdrop of continued credit growth.
Crisil expects bank credit growth of 14.5–15.5% in FY27, with MSME and retail lending remaining key drivers.
Corporate credit growth is expected to receive support from continued substitution of bank loans by the bond market and greater utilisation of working-capital limits.
A rate increase could extend this substitution until bank lending rates adjust to the higher policy environment.
Crisil expects banks to maintain stable credit profiles, supported by strong capitalisation and resilient asset quality.
